source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Heater and Air Conditioning, p.1A-18

procedures.title: Refrigeration system: maintaining chemical stability
steps: Cap any refrigerant or gauge line as soon as it is disconnected.
Keep tools, the gauge set and replacement parts clean and dry.
Use a very clean, dry container when adding oil; open the oil container only when ready and recap it right after use, since the oil absorbs moisture quickly.
Before opening a system, have everything ready so it stays open as briefly as possible.
After the work is done and the system resealed, evacuate air and moisture before recharging.

procedures.title: J-8393 charging station: description
notes: A portable unit combining a vacuum pump, refrigerant supply, gauges, valves and a 5 pound metering charging cylinder (see figure 24 in the manual).
Refrigerant is metered by volume, so no scales or hot-water pails are needed and the exact charge can be added; the unit stays plumbed, so no refrigerant is lost purging and hooking up.
Use comes down to attaching two hoses and working clearly labeled valves. The dealer's own vacuum pump, gauges and manifold can be used with it.

procedures.title: Gauge set: description
notes: The gauge set (see figure 25 in the manual) is part of the J-8393 station and is used for purging, evacuating, charging and diagnosis.

The left gauge is the low pressure gauge, reading pressure (psi) and vacuum (inches); always use it on the low side. A healthy system never drops below 0 psi on the low side, but some faults pull it into vacuum.
The high pressure gauge reads the high side.
The manifold hand valves do not shut off pressure to the gauges; they only close each port to the center connector and to each other. Keep them closed for most diagnosis and service.
